correctness.rationale: Integrating nodal hats gives the positive-definite Gram matrix in RESULT; each kernel evaluation row is represented by the corresponding coordinates of the inverse. For an arbitrary evaluation point the row is a convex combination of the adjacent nodal rows. The alternating nodal signs hold on the full open parameter interval by the displayed coefficients. An independent symbolic reconstruction used the signed integral 1 (the projector fixes constants) plus twice the negative triangle areas to recover E, S and C. E−S has a strictly positive numerator after removing the common positive denominator, and E−C changes sign once with 2ε²+11ε−5. C strictly decreases; the endpoint derivative has the stated all-positive numerator after factoring its positive denominator. This gives the switch and unique minimizer (√161−11)/4 with norm 4/3+√161/21, limits 7/3 and 22/9, and C>2 iff ε<1/3. At each maximizing knot the input sign of the kernel attains the norm; continuity identifies the output essential supremum with its true maximum, including at endpoints. Even interior evaluation points cannot add norming locations because each mesh interval has at least one strictly submaximal shoulder endpoint.
residual_risks: The one-sided limits concern distinct-knot spaces and are not norms computed by merging knots. The minimizer is only within the symmetric one-parameter family.

value.rationale: The symmetric path permits clustering at either the center or both boundaries. A uniform stability constant cannot decide the best mesh or even whether the boundaries or center dominate. Their competing monotone branches, below-two optimal amplification, and distinct above-two clustering limits answer a concrete, minimal mesh-design question for the standard least-squares projector.
residual_risks: No nonsymmetric or higher-degree knot optimization follows.
